title: Rabbi Zakkai (an Amora)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman infers that apparently he was Shmuel’s student, as in [Yevamot 67a:11-12](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.67a.11-12): Shmuel said to Rav Chana of Baghdad … Rabbi Zakkai sat; in [Eruvin 49a:17](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.49a.17) Rabbi Abba spoke to Rav Yehudah at the press in Rav Zakkai’s house; and in [Sanhedrin 70a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.70a.21), Mar Ukva speaks in the name of Rabbi Zakkai.

Afterward he went up to the Land of Israel and was the reciter of baraitot in Rabbi Yochanan’s academy, as in Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat, beginning of chapter 7: “Rabbi Zakkai taught before Rabbi Yochanan: He slaughtered, he burned [incense] … Rabbi Yochanan said to him: Babylonian, you crossed three rivers on your way and came out broken — he is liable only once.” So it is in [Sanhedrin 62a:5-6](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.62a.5-6): “Rabbi Zakkai taught before Rabbi Yochanan: He slaughtered … He said to him: Go out and teach it outside.” Likewise in Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 8:3 he taught before Rabbi Yochanan, “The daughter of an Ammonite convert is fit,” and Rabbi Yochanan said to him, “Babylonian, you crossed three rivers on your way and came out broken”; Hyman cites [Yevamot 77b:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.77b.1) as a parallel and gives Rabbi Yochanan’s reply: “Go out and teach it outside.”[^4] Likewise in [Eruvin 9a:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.9a.6): “Rabbi Zakkai taught before Rabbi Yochanan: Between side-posts … He said to him: Go out and teach it outside.”

In [Niddah 41b:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.41b.12) and Jerusalem Talmud Yoma, chapter 6, end of halakhah 6: “Rabbi Zakkai taught.” In Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 4:3 Rabbi Zakkai expounded: “And you shall dwell in the field — and My presence in the field.” From there he sent to Mar Ukva concerning a law of an oath, as in [Ketubot 87a:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.87a.8).

notes.text: Saved Guggenheimer Shabbat7:1 has ואיתברת, you were broken, not the rivers broke. The source’s first עבדת is read in the parallel עברת sense. Tanna here is a baraita reciter in the Amoraic academy; חייב אחת means liable once. Chapter/halakhah references are Jerusalem Talmud.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 7:1 directly has Zakkai teaching Yochanan, the rebuke that he himself came out broken, and liability once. The inferred apprenticeship to Shmuel and the collected migration narrative are Hyman’s; recitation of a baraita does not establish a Mishnaic identity.

The consulted [Sanhedrin 70a:21](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.70a.21) presents two attributions for the Noah interpretation. The second is the chain Hyman cites, Mar Ukva in Rabbi Zakkai’s name. [Heilprin’s corresponding notice](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1133&lang=en) records that chain and the oath ruling sent to Mar Ukva.

In Yevamot 67a Shmuel speaks to Rav Chana, and Zakkai raises an objection in the next passage. Hyman infers that Zakkai was Shmuel’s student. At Yevamot 77b Zakkai recites a baraita and Rabbi Yochanan answers with a different interpretation. The linked Sanhedrin and Eruvin passages use the words “Go out and teach it outside.”
